ai.title: Gate knowledge file generation on existing files
ai.summary: mainPrompt.ts adds a `hasKnowledgeFiles` check before spawning `generateKnowledgeFiles`. This prevents the system from attempting to create knowledge files in projects that don't already have them, aligning with the rule to only generate changes for existing files.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer try to create summary notes for projects that don't already have them, saving a step in projects that haven't set up those notes yet. This only affects projects that did not already have the summary notes to begin with, so if you work on a project that already had them, nothing changes for you. The change is live today.

ai.title: Redo CLI help menu
ai.summary: The CLI help menu in npm-app/src/menu.ts was redone to improve clarity and reduce noise. The initial prompt in npm-app/src/cli.ts had its emoji removed. The help text now separates 'ASK MANICODE TO...' examples from 'COMMANDS', and the 'Welcome' message was simplified.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now prints a cleaner two-part greeting: a short welcome line followed by a single sentence explaining that the assistant will read and write files in your current folder and run commands in your terminal. The old help menu mixed these instructions together with example requests and shortcut keys in one block; the new menu splits them into separate sections labeled with headings, so the example requests ("Ask Manicode to...") appear apart from the keyboard shortcuts. The waving-hand emoji that used to appear in the first prompt was also removed, leaving plain text. If you launch the tool today, you will see this tidier layout the moment it starts.

ai.title: main-prompt distinguishes Creating from Editing
ai.summary: main-prompt.ts now checks file existence via requestFile before formatting the status line, outputting Creating for new files and Editing for existing ones. This replaces the previous hardcoded Editing label. Scope: backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Mechanism relies on requestFile returning null for missing files to determine isNewFile.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create or open a file, you'll now see "Creating file" in the status line if it's a brand-new file, instead of always seeing "Editing file" like before. The assistant now checks whether a file already exists before showing that message, so it can tell the difference between making a new file and working on an existing one. This affects how the assistant reports its progress when you're working with files in the backend.

ai.title: Add usage tracking and billing infrastructure
ai.summary: Implemented initial usage tracking via new `fingerprint` and `message` DB tables in `backend/src/billing/message.ts` and migrations `0002`/`0003`. The system now calculates costs per model (Sonnet, Haiku, GPT-4o) using defined token prices and a 20% profit margin, storing detailed request/response metadata and quota states. Authentication flows were updated to store `fingerprintId` and hashes in session rows, with CLI polling for credentials instead of direct backend pushes. This change introduces core billing logic to `common/src/db/schema` and updates `backend/src/claude.ts` to pass session context for accurate cost attribution.

eli5.text: Starting October 2024, the system now tracks how much you've used the AI assistant and assigns a cost to it based on the model type (Claude or GPT) and the length of your prompt and responses. Your usage is tied to your session, so each conversation you have is recorded for potential future billing. You won't see direct charges today, but the infrastructure to calculate costs, like $3 per million input tokens for Claude Sonnet, is now in place and running behind the scenes. This affects anyone signing in through the CLI tool (npm-app), as the new flow requires your credentials to be polled rather than pushed directly.

The software got a new release number, which means the team packaged up several recent improvements and made them available for you to install. Among the bundled changes, you can now see clearer guidance when you ask the assistant for help, the assistant better tells the difference between starting a new document and editing an existing one, and the tool can start tracking how much it is being used for billing purposes. A couple of behind-the-scenes adjustments also make sure the helper menu and document-generation steps behave more predictably. If you update to this release, your installed copy will match the latest set of fixes and features the team has been working on.

ai.title: Fix deploy:npm-app script to use cd npm-app && npm publish
ai.summary: Updated `deploy:npm-app` script in `package.json`. Replaced `bun --cwd npm publish` with `cd npm-app && npm publish`. Ensures correct directory context and npm binary usage for publishing.

eli5.text: The internal script that publishes the npm package had a small bug where it was using the wrong tool to navigate into the project folder before uploading. That step has been fixed so it changes into the correct folder first and then publishes using the standard npm tool, preventing the deployment from failing or publishing from the wrong location.

ai.title: Fix db migration snapshot default expressions
ai.summary: Corrected timestamp column default expressions in `common/src/db/migrations/meta/0003_snapshot.json` by removing invalid `SELECT` prefixes from `now() + INTERVAL '1 month'`. Drizzle Kit snapshots expect raw SQL expressions, not query statements, causing metadata validation mismatches. Affects shared core database migration metadata only.

eli5.text: If you were to look at the date a record is set to expire on, it would now show the correct calculation instead of a broken one that included an extra keyword it shouldn't have. This is just a behind-the-scenes fix to the system's internal notes about how dates are calculated, so there's nothing you need to do, it's already working correctly today.
